claim: A preregistered adversarial collaboration found results aligning with some predictions of IIT and GNWT while substantially challenging key tenets of both biological implementations.
method: Preregistered, multi-site adversarial collaboration using fMRI, MEG, and intracranial EEG with 256 human participants; published 2025-04-30.
limitations: The experiment tested selected predictions and biological implementations, not every mathematical or computational core claim.
The stimuli and outcomes concern human visual consciousness and do not directly validate an AI-consciousness test.
Some regions and modalities had uneven sampling, and the paper reports both aligned and challenging results.

claim: Theory-derived computational indicators offer a rigorous way to assess AI systems; the report did not identify the assessed current systems as conscious and found no obvious technical barrier to future systems satisfying the indicators.
method: Interdisciplinary review deriving computational indicator properties from several neuroscientific theories and applying them to selected AI systems; report published 2023-08-17.
limitations: Indicator properties inherit uncertainty and disagreement from the underlying theories.
Satisfying indicators would be evidence to assess, not by itself proof of subjective experience.
The surveyed systems and technical state reflect a 2023 snapshot.

claim: Organizations doing advanced AI research need precautionary policies for assessing possible AI consciousness, phased development, external consultation, controlled knowledge sharing, and uncertainty-aware public communication.
method: Normative analysis proposing five principles for responsible AI-consciousness research; Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research article published in 2025.
limitations: The principles are normative governance recommendations, not empirical evidence that any AI system is conscious.
Implementation details and enforcement mechanisms require institution-specific design and external review.
The feasibility and timing of conscious AI remain uncertain.

claim: The preservation risk-register repository artifact satisfies its checked-in schema and received independent exact-head agent review plus a successful pinned local-model review.
method: Pull request 116 ran typecheck, tests, strategy verification, proposal review, exact-head independent agent review 4848516713, and pinned local-model workflow run 30852585749 before merge as 882d62fdd3144be9a9ce8c81b74348b121b0c39e.
limitations: This evidence verifies a repository artifact and its review provenance, not reduced real-world risk, external deployment, institutional adoption, or the correctness of future risk forecasts.
The source rankings remain uncertainty-bearing public-information assessments that require future evidence refreshes.
